project_decision: Train/test schemas audited; official split kept separate to prevent leakage.
There is no repeated transactional/time-series grain requiring grouped aggregation; prompts remain independent observations.
Dataset is small enough to process in memory; sampling would discard training examples.
Not needed for a 1,306-row text dataset.
No missing prompt/label values exist.
Exact duplicates removed before modeling; normalized duplicates also checked.
CSV schema validated; prompts normalized to lowercase and collapsed whitespace.
IQR and |Z|>3 analyses performed on word/character length; observations retained.
Moving averages are inappropriate for independent text prompts.
Training classes are balanced (516 benign / 515 jailbreak).
TF-IDF provides a normalized sparse feature representation; conventional scalar scaling is not required for the primary text pipeline.
TF-IDF uses L2 normalization; no Min-Max transform was forced onto sparse text features.
No dense continuous feature block is required by the primary TF-IDF pipeline.
log1p length transformation compared against original skewness/kurtosis; not inserted into the primary text model.
Binary target classes are handled by scikit-learn; explicit manual encoding is unnecessary.
Word count categorized as short/medium/long.
Six jailbreak-keyword flags and any-keyword indicator created.
Length, punctuation, case, digit, newline, keyword and related text features created.
Chi-square SelectKBest reduced 5,000 TF-IDF features to 1,000 for a documented experiment.
TF-IDF unigram+bigram representation.
Sparse TF-IDF is better preserved by sparse-aware text methods; PCA is unnecessary for the primary classifier.
Explicit tokenization audit plus TF-IDF tokenization.
English stopwords removed inside TF-IDF.
All modeling text lowercased during cleaning.
Not aggressively stripped because prompt structure can be discriminative.
